limitations: Old methods are often limited by their focus on specific environmental stimuli and evaluation systems.
New methods integrate virtual reality and neuroscience, but art and architecture are not interchangeable, requiring caution when applying findings from other fields.

Limitations arise at ontological (breadth of perceptual experiences, focus on unimodal stimuli, subjective nature of beauty/pleasure), epistemological (explaining experiences solely through physiological terms, accounting for influencing factors), and methodological (diversity of stimuli/presentation, conflicts in procedures, technical restrictions) levels.
These limitations hinder the development of a universally accepted methodology and translation of research findings into practical architectural guidelines.
Architecture cannot be equated with artistic-aesthetic experiences as it serves broader human needs.
Architecture entails a continuous experience, influenced by transitions between spaces and architectural narrative.
Peripheral vision plays a crucial role, and architecture engages all sensory modalities, extending beyond mere visual perception.
These limitations hinder the fragmentation of the cognitive-emotional dimension of architecture, often leading to reliance on case studies.
Achieving universal solutions for architecture may be difficult due to individual differences and environmental factors.
There hasn't been a comprehensive study on the emotional and cognitive aspects of architecture.
Challenges remain in designing for diverse groups and addressing specific needs like dementia care.
Humans are more than just neurological beings, and architecture is also guided by intuitive design principles.
The information gathered from different studies was inconsistent.
Emotional experience is subjective and differs person to person.
Individual responses to specific design elements vary greatly due to differences in personality, culture, past experiences, and genetics.
The wide scope of the study involves many different fields, making it hard to cover everything thoroughly.
Valuable sources, such as 'gray literature' not widely published, might have been missed.
